newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Central African Republic calm after shooting.
newsitem.headline: Central African Republic calm after shooting.

text.p: Calm returned to the Central African Republic capital Bangui on Tuesday after clashes between troops loyal to President Ange-Felix Patasse and mutinous soldiers, witnesses said.
Shooting continued overnight but subsided at dawn.

Earlier Interior Minister Jean Willybiro-Sacko said 12 members of the security forces and three civilians had been wounded in Monday's clashes, which followed the break-up of a march by civilians demanding that Patasse resign.
Some witnesses and the rebels spoke of up to four deaths. The government formally denied the reports.
The impoverished Central African nation is in the grip of its third army mutiny within a year. Four African leaders sent by a Franco-African summit negotiated a truce this month.
French troops, stationed in Bangui, intervened in May under a defence pact to keep Patasse in power.
The mutinies, which began in April, were initially over pay but developed into demands, backed by the opposition, that Patasse step down. The latest revolt began in mid-November.
Patasse, elected in 1993, has dismissed the demands as unconstitutional. The mutiny has turned into bloody feuding between his Baya tribe and Yakomas who dominate rebel ranks.
Mutineers control suburbs of the capital while loyalists and French troops control the centre.
